subject: Cooking
title: Vietnamese Egg Coffee: Necessity as Invention
description: One-minute skill: Vietnamese Egg Coffee: Necessity as Invention.

hook.text: When milk was scarce in 1940s Hanoi, a bartender whipped egg yolks with sugar and poured coffee over them.

buildup.text: Nguyen Van Giang at Café Giang created cà phê trứng — egg coffee — as a wartime milk substitute.

discovery.text: Whipped egg yolks create a rich, custard-like layer that floats on dark Vietnamese drip coffee — tiramisu in a cup.

twist.text: The café is still family-run today, in a Hanoi alley — unchanged for 75 years, serving the original recipe.

climax.text: Egg coffee has spread to specialty cafés worldwide — what started from scarcity became a global delicacy.

punchline.text: No milk? No problem. Genius is what happens when you work with what you have.

quiz.question: Why was Vietnamese egg coffee invented?

details.summary: Vietnamese egg coffee was invented in 1946 by Nguyen Van Giang in Hanoi when a milk shortage forced him to substitute whipped egg yolk with condensed milk and sugar. The resulting drink is a creamy, custard-like layer floating on strong Vietnamese coffee.
details.whyItMatters: Egg coffee demonstrates how scarcity drives culinary innovation. A wartime milk shortage produced a drink that became a Hanoi icon now sought by tourists worldwide.
takeaways: Invented during a 1946 milk shortage in Hanoi
Whipped egg yolk with condensed milk creates a custard-like layer
The original Café Giang still serves the recipe in Hanoi today

faq.question: What does Vietnamese egg coffee taste like?
faq.answer: The top layer tastes like liquid tiramisu or crème brûlée — rich, sweet, and custardy from whipped egg yolk and condensed milk. Below it sits strong, dark Vietnamese robusta coffee. Sipping through the creamy layer into bitter coffee creates a changing flavor experience with every sip.

faq.question: Is it safe to drink raw egg in coffee?
faq.answer: The egg yolk is vigorously whipped with hot condensed milk and sugar, partially cooking it through emulsification and heat. The hot coffee further raises the temperature. Using fresh, quality eggs minimizes risk. In Hanoi, millions of cups are consumed annually without issues.
